profile.headline: Software Developer at Epic | BS Computer Science at UTD '23
profile.summary:
I graduated from the University of Texas Dallas with my Bachelor's of Science in Computer Science in spring 2023 and now  work for Epic Systems as a Software Developer. I have experience working with medium size companies like Varis and Summit Financial Group which both offered me the ability to see the whole tech stack and understand their systems at a high level. Outside of work, I have spent the last several years at UTD studying the theory of Computer Science and have begun being an active part of leadership for UTD Nebula Labs, an organization on campus which seeks to help students build software that helps other students. 

Beyond my professional life, I like to spend my time outdoors and with friends. I do lots of hiking and would like to visit all of the National Parks some day!

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: Work on full stack development building healthcare infrastructure systems. Work in C#, Typescript, React, and M Programming Language to solve complex problems through collaboration and direct communication with clients.

positions.title: SDE Intern
positions.description: Help build B2B services as a full stack development intern. Work in a full team experience collaborating with senior developers and engineers to build services with Varis business value.
positions.insights: Go (Programming Language), Cross-functional Coordination and +2 skills

positions.title: CRM Development Intern
positions.description: Develop and manage a small but complex CRM/ ERP solution for a mid-sized organization in a professional setting.
positions.insights: Microsoft Power BI, Cross-functional Coordination and +1 skill

positions.title: Service Technician/ Crew Cheif
positions.description: As a service tech I replaced, repaired, and maintained wheels and tires for customers. Provided customer service and worked in a stressful team environment. As a crew chief I helped managed workflow of a work cell by preparing vehicles for service and helping instruct service technicians.

educations.schoolName: The University of Texas at Dallas

volunteerExperiences.description: I helped found Nebula Labs as an organization to help teach students at the University of Texas at Dallas how to build impactful software and the value of using your talents to give back to your community. I served as a project lead, Vice President, and President during my time with the organization.

I served as both an administrative staff and administrative department head. This entailed managing camp paperwork for both staff and participant as well as delivering long-form presentations for the camp program. As a department head I also took up responsibility of managing my staff's workflow and communicating with other camp departments to deliver the best experience to camp participants.
